From time to time, certain groups on social sites need to be able to communicate with each other more directly than the voting system or private messaging allows.

Examples...

  • administrator announcements that need to be seen sitewide
  • moderator announcements where they poll the people of a verse for feedback on rules changes
  • curated content created for an individual verse (such as a 'best of 2014' contest result)
  • live update threads, such as an ongoing major news event in a news community
  • active AMAs from various noteworthy public figures
  • advertisements (not that I'm advocating for advertisements, this is just an example)

Historically, these sorts of things have always been handled with 'sticky' threads, or with submissions that temporarily occupy the top spot.

All of the implementations of these various 'active' threads have always been pretty damn awful. As examples...

  • admin notices that are not upvoted and noticed, resulting in users unaware of changes
  • mod announcements being completely ignored or heavily downvoted - this also extends to mod comments
  • curated submissions also being ignored, despite being something the community desires
  • live update threads becoming fragmented and hard to follow, even hard to find
  • AMAs taking off late, sometimes even after the public figure has run out of time
  • advertisements being shown to the same users multiple times despite them having no interest

Sticky threads on reddit are insultingly worthless. They get fewer votes (people think the votes aren't needed), and are only visible when visiting a subreddit directly. They seldom, if ever, reach high enough in a subscriber's feed to be noticed by anything even approaching a majority of a community's subscribers. This means that it is impossible to reliably conduct a democratic vote on important issues facing any given community.

I'd like to propose that all of these problems are in fact the SAME, and can be handled with a single unified system.

What we're discussing here is giving special meaning to the TOP submission slot on any given page on whoaverse.

I think this should be a rotating whirlwind of special threads from all of the above categories, no matter where on whoaverse a person is.

The key difference here, is that a user is to be shown these special threads ONLY ONE TIME EACH.

This is sufficient to make a subscriber aware of issues in his verses, to let admins reach all users, to publicize AMAs and curated content threads in a timely manner, and to rotate advertisements intelligently IF whoaverse ever goes that way.

The key points of treating each of these differently...

  • admin threads, AMA threads displayed once to each user while they are active/relevant
  • mod/curated/live threads displayed once to each user, but only for subverses where they are subscribed
  • advertisements only ever shown once to each user, and with verse-specific targeting (again, if whoaverse ever goes that way)
  • allow users to OPT OUT of AMAs and live threads in their profiles if they choose to do so, but default to in
  • adding new categories of posts to this rotation is easy in the future as the site evolves

If subverses try to abuse this system to spam people, the solution is simple, unsubscribe from subverses with crappy moderation teams and let them die out.

This solves several core problems with reddit that they don't even understand properly. It does so with a single elegant system that can be extended to support any number of future categories, and it does it in a way provides consequences for verses that abuse it.

Edit: I'd also like to suggest extending this functionality into its own special page. Something like /v/all, only this might be better titled as /v/special. This allows people to see all of the hot button 'live' or 'feeedback' threads active on whoaverse at once. This one would obviously be devoid of the advertisements.

The UI for this should be incredibly simple.

Under each submission (probably limited to self-posts only, just like reddit) there should appear a single word... 'publish'. That flags the post for inclusion in this rotating system. There should only be at most one publicized thread per verse, just like the sticky threads on reddit.

It could also 'sticky' this content at the top of the local verse, but this doesn't need to happen. It doesn't work very well for reddit. If this system works effectively, publicized threads should gain upvotes on their own merits quickly enough.
